OGTR named the council area this site is in and published no coordinate on the page this was read from, so this marker sits in that council area and not at the trial itself. WHY IT MATTERS. OGTR names the council area of every licensed site, its area in hectares and the licence it runs under. No other register on this map states where a release is at all, which is the comparison worth making even at this resolution.

-81.89720,26.51510.name: Southwest Florida Fertility Center, PA
-81.89720,26.51510.desc: A fertility clinic reporting to the CDC's National ART Surveillance System. Medical director: Jacob L. Glock, MD. A fertility clinic is where human embryos are made, selected and stored, and where assisted reproduction happens, like IVF, ICSI, egg and sperm donation, freezing embryos and eggs for later. Reporting is required of every US clinic performing assisted reproduction, under the Fertility Clinic Success Rate and Certification Act, so this is close to a complete register rather than a list of members. What it records is cycles started, which is not the same as children born.

-96.17565,43.07969.name: Innovations Through Research, LLC.
-96.17565,43.07969.desc: An organisation accredited by AAALAC International for its care and use of laboratory animals. Part of Argenta US Holdings Inc.. Accreditation is voluntary and paid for, so this is a list of organisations that chose to be inspected rather than a register of everyone doing the work. An organisation absent from it is not accredited; that says nothing about whether it uses animals. In several countries the largest users are absent for exactly that reason. The directory gives a city and country and no street address, so this point marks where the organisation is registered rather than the building where animals are held.

-122.91312,49.20368.desc: An institution certified by the Canadian Council on Animal Care for its use of animals in science. Certificate of GAP Last visit: regular, March 2026. -122.14000,37.41800.name: Pacific Biosciences
-122.14000,37.41800.desc: Long-read sequencing, which reads DNA in longer continuous stretches than short-read platforms and so detects structural changes that short reads miss — including unintended insertions at an edit site. The verification capability and the editing capability come from the same industry.

-122.14000,37.41800.name: Ohalo Genetics
-122.14000,37.41800.desc: Working on making crops produce seed that breeds true rather than segregating, which would let farmers replant hybrids. The same technique would also let a company keep a variety uniform without hybrid seed sales, and which use it gets put to has not been settled.

121.59000,31.20000.name: Shanghai Model Organisms Center
121.59000,31.20000.desc: A Chinese supplier of engineered mice and rats, serving a research system whose scale now rivals the American one. China publishes no national count of animals used in research, so the size of the practice is inferred from suppliers rather than reported.

11.77000,55.51000.name: DLF Seeds
11.77000,55.51000.desc: A Danish cooperative that is the world's largest supplier of grass and clover seed, for pasture, forage and turf. Grassland covers more of the planet's agricultural area than any crop and receives almost none of the attention: a seed sector this large sits outside the entire engineered-crop argument because nobody has found it worth engineering.

-1.52000,12.37000.name: Institut de l’Environnement et de Recherches Agricoles
-1.52000,12.37000.desc: Burkina Faso grew Bt cotton commercially and then withdrew it, after the fibre came out shorter and buyers paid less. The trait worked against the pest and the crop lost value anyway — which is the clearest demonstration on this map that a trait doing what it says is not the same as a product that works.
